record_type_quote:
To further
explore this topic, we replicated the design framework established by
Janssen and colleagues (2008), using a new set of stimuli and integrating
EEG into the design in order to investigate the research question
whether the production of Mandarin compound words is influenced by
morpheme or compound frequency in the present study.

targets.authors: Janssen, N., Bi, Y., & Caramazza, A.
targets.title: A tale of two frequencies: Determining the speed of lexical access for Mandarin Chinese and English compounds.

targets.outcome_quote:
Interestingly, the reaction times across conditions in our study did
not align with the earlier findings of Janssen and colleagues (2008).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The new naming experiment reverses the original frequency pattern: constituent frequency influences response time and whole-word frequency does not. The authors explicitly state disagreement with Janssen et al. EEG is an extension rather than an agreeing replication test.

reasoning: New participants and new stimuli retest Janssen et al. (2008), with EEG added. Other theoretical and task references are background.
